title: Malaria Severity Risk Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Escalate immediately when malaria presentations include altered mental status, respiratory distress, severe anemia, or inability to tolerate oral therapy.
Use severity assessment to separate uncomplicated malaria from inpatient or ICU pathways early.
Review pregnancy, age, and species pattern when interpreting severity and treatment urgency.

title: Malaria Exposure Risk Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Use exposure history, household clustering, and symptom onset to prioritize malaria contact follow-up.
Escalate contacts with fever, pregnancy, very young age, or delayed presentation for prompt testing.
Tie risk scoring to testing and prophylaxis policy rather than exposure labels alone.

title: TB Contact Risk Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Prioritize TB contact risk by exposure intensity, symptoms, HIV status, and age-related vulnerability.
Escalate symptomatic or immunocompromised contacts for urgent evaluation rather than routine follow-up.
Pair contact risk scoring with preventive therapy and testing pathways.

title: CKD Staging Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Interpret CKD risk using eGFR and albuminuria together rather than isolated renal function values.
Escalate advanced CKD, rapidly declining function, or heavy albuminuria for nephrology-directed management.
Link staging output to blood pressure, renal-protective therapy, and follow-up interval decisions.

title: PMTCT Risk Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Escalate PMTCT risk when viral suppression, adherence, timing of ART, or infant prophylaxis planning is uncertain.
Treat PMTCT risk as a maternal-infant pathway issue rather than a standalone maternal score.
Document transmission-risk drivers explicitly so follow-up and counseling are targeted.

title: SOFA Score Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Use SOFA as a deterioration and organ-support escalation signal, not as a replacement for clinician assessment.
Trend SOFA over time and respond to worsening trajectories rather than isolated scores alone.
Escalate immediately when multi-organ dysfunction or sepsis suspicion is rising.

title: Suicide Risk Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Escalate suicide risk immediately when intent, plan, recent behavior, or inability to maintain safety is present.
Treat suicide risk assessment as a crisis pathway requiring follow-up disposition, not just a severity label.
Document protective factors and near-term safety actions alongside the risk level.

title: Cholera Risk Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Escalate cholera risk when dehydration features, hypotension, or inability to drink are present.
Use cholera risk scoring to drive rehydration pathway intensity and outbreak notification urgency.
Pair risk output with infection-control and public-health action, not treatment advice alone.
